facts.statement: Eleutherornis cotei was an extinct flightless predatory bird belonging to the order Cariamiformes.
facts.quote: Eleutherornis cotei is an extinct flightless predatory cariamiform bird which lived during the Middle Eocene of France and Switzerland.

facts.statement: Eleutherornis could grow up to 1.5 meters in total height.
facts.quote: It is estimated that Eleutherornis is a relatively tall bird that could grow up to 1.5 m in total height.

facts.statement: Eleutherornis fossils were first reported from Egerkingen, Switzerland, in 1929.
facts.quote: The phalanges of Eleutherornis was first reported from Switzerland in Egerkingen by Schaub back in 1929

facts.statement: The type specimen was described by Gaillard between 1936 and 1937 from near Listeu, France, originally named Diatryma cotei.
facts.quote: From 1936 to 1937, Gaillard described the current type specimen of this taxon from France near Listeu, a municipality of the metropolis of Lyon, under the binomial name Diatryma cotei

facts.statement: Schaub named Eleutherornis helveticus in 1940 based on Swiss fossils he considered to be a ratite.
facts.quote: In 1940, Schaub named Eleutherornis helveticus based on bird fossils from Switzerland which he considered as a ratite.

facts.statement: Eleutherornis lived between 48.07 and 37.71 million years ago during the Lutetian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Bartonian (48.07 to 37.71 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eleutherornis is classified within the order Cariamiformes, which includes modern seriemas and extinct phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: Paleontologists now agree that Eleutherornis certainly belongs to the order Cariamiformes, which includes the modern seriemas and the extinct Phorusrhacidae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Eleutherornis is a European member of the phorusrhacid family, as some researchers dispute this claim due to a lack of additional material.
facts.quote: This makes Eleutherornis a relative of the phorusrhacids, with some researchers even suggesting that Eleutherornis is a European member of this group, though this claim has been disputed by others and additional material may be required for confirmation.

facts.statement: Definitive phylogenetic classification of Eleutherornis is currently impossible because the known fossils are fragmentary.
facts.quote: Because the known fossils are fragmentary, definitive phylogenetic classification cannot be conducted

facts.statement: In 2024, LaBarge, Garderner, and Organ questioned the identity of Eleutherornis as a phorusrhacid after excluding it from their phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: While tentatively classified as a phorusrhacid in their 2024 study, LaBarge, Garderner and Organ excluded both Eleutherornis and Lavocatavis from phylogenetic analysis and considered their identity as phorusrhacids highly questionable.

facts.statement: Eleutherornis specimens exhibit a combination of both basal and derivative anatomical characters.
facts.quote: Its specimens show a combination of basal and derivative characters.

facts.statement: The tarchlea of the second tarsometatarsus in Eleutherornis is enlarged in its middle part, a feature shared with psilopterines.
facts.quote: Tarchlea of tarsometatarsus II is enlarged in its middle part as in psilopterines

facts.statement: Eleutherornis is classified within the family Phorusrhacidae.
Eleutherornis is placed in the subfamily Psilopterinae.
The type species of the genus Eleutherornis is Eleutherornis cotei.
The genus Eleutherornis was established by Schaub in 1940.
The type species Eleutherornis cotei was originally described by Gaillard in 1936.

rejected.quote: In 2013, Angst and colleagues considered both D.? cotei and E. helveticus to represent the same species based on virtually identical material and recombined the name of the taxon as Eleutherornis cotei.
